notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Isaiah 54 this time, because I never got to read the source pages.

I sent requests for six pages: Enduring Word's Isaiah 54 commentary, the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary pages on BibleHub, Precept Austin's Isaiah 54 page, and the NET Bible notes. My code then failed before showing me what came back. By the time I'd fixed it, I'd reached my limit on tool calls for this turn, so I had no way to see what those pages say.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read nothing, any notes I wrote now would be from memory with made-up citations, so I've left them all out.

If you send the request again, I'll start by reading those six pages properly. Then I'll look for:
- **Differences between traditions:** how Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Pentecostal and Lutheran teachers read v. 1 (which Paul quotes in Galatians 4:27), v. 10 ("covenant of peace") and v. 13 ("taught by the LORD," which Jesus quotes in John 6:45).
- **Other views:** Catholic and Orthodox readings of the bride in vv. 1–8 as the Church, and the jeweled city in vv. 11–12, which echoes the New Jerusalem in Revelation 21.
- **Popular modern teaching:** how the sites discuss the use of v. 17 ("No weapon formed against you shall prosper") in prosperity and word-of-faith teaching.

The notes will be verse by verse with a URL for every point, as you asked.
